Dhaka, all day

Seven kilometres an hour

That is how fast this city moves now. A decade ago it was three times quicker. Keep scrolling and you will cover more ground than the traffic below you.

A car loses this race

One kilometre, at the speeds people actually travel through the worst corridor at the worst hour of the day. Watch it happen in real time.

Both markers move at their true speeds. The race restarts by itself.

The city breathes twice a day

Every spoke is one hour. The longer and greener it reaches, the faster the roads are running. Dhaka falls apart before nine in the morning, half recovers over lunch, then sinks again and stays there until well past ten at night.

crawling slow moving clear

The jam has a spine

Colour the main corridors by how fast they run at the peak and one route stands out, running the length of the city from Uttara down to Motijheel. When one link seizes, the ones beside it follow within minutes.

Now stand in it

This is a live simulation, not a video. Every vehicle below decides its own speed from the gap in front of it, the way real drivers do. Move the slider to change the hour and watch the road fill, seize, and slowly clear.

Which road

So what does it take from you?

Pick the road you travel most. Every square below is one day of your year, and the pale ones are the days you spend sitting still.

17
days a year

That is 412 hours, every year, spent going nowhere on this one stretch of road.

365 days. The pale squares are yours to lose.

Between midnight and five, it is a different city

For five hours a night the roads carry what they were built to carry, and Dhaka runs at twenty-five kilometres an hour. Then the sun comes up.
